title: Metamorphic Relation Tolerance
description: Schema for metamorphic relation (MR) tolerance definitions in the PROJ-036 Prompt Regression Test Harness. MR tolerances specify the maximum permissible score delta between transformed and original inputs, along with statistical parameters for significance testing. These are the oracle-safe assertions that solve the LLM test oracle problem without requiring exact expected outputs.

name.description: Human-readable name for this metamorphic relation.

version.description: Contract version for this MR tolerance specification.

agent.description: The agent(s) this MR tolerance applies to.

definition.description: Precise definition of this metamorphic relation: what transformation is applied, what consistency property is expected.

transformation.description: Specification of the input transformation applied for this MR.

applies_to.description: Which part of the input is transformed.

preservation_requirement.description: What semantic property is preserved by the transformation (semantic meaning, intent, factual content, etc.).

transformation_generator.description: Optional: how the transformation is generated (e.g., 'secondary LLM call', 'deterministic rule', 'template substitution').

transformation_variants.description: For MRs with multiple transformation variants (e.g., MR-004 has multiple formatting styles): list of variant names.

expected_direction.description: Expected direction of the score difference between transformed and original. NEUTRAL means the transformation should not change quality. DECREASE means quality should decrease (MR-002 when negating quality constraints). CHANGE means quality should change in some direction (used when direction depends on what is negated).

max_delta.description: Maximum permissible absolute score difference between transformed and original input quality scores (|score_original - score_transformed|). Only relevant when expected_direction is NEUTRAL.

min_detectable_change.description: Minimum expected score difference for MRs where the transformation is expected to produce a change (expected_direction is DECREASE, INCREASE, or CHANGE). Only relevant for MR-002.

max_delta_rationale.description: Statistical and empirical rationale for the chosen max_delta value. Must reference the LLM non-determinism baseline (0.02-0.04) and the LLMORPH false positive rate (8.6% at similar tolerances).

p_value_threshold.description: Significance threshold for the Wilcoxon signed-rank test applied to MR comparison. Standard: 0.05. Higher values (0.10) are used for exploratory warnings.

minimum_sample_size.description: Minimum number of input-output pairs required for valid MR comparison. Below this threshold, MR results are labeled INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE and not used for regression classification.

recommended_sample_size.description: Recommended sample size for reliable MR comparison. Provides sufficient statistical power for the specified effect size threshold.

effect_size_threshold.description: Cohen's r effect size threshold (derived from Wilcoxon Z / sqrt(N)) above which a violation is classified as REGRESSION rather than MARGINAL. Typical values: 0.25 (small-to-medium), 0.30 (medium), 0.40 (large).

violation_condition.description: Precise conditions that must ALL be met to declare an MR violation.

conditions.description: List of individual conditions that combine to define a violation.

expression.description: Formal expression of the condition in pseudocode.

combination_logic.description: How conditions are combined: 'ALL' (all must be true), 'ANY' (any single condition triggers violation), or custom expression referencing condition_ids.

violation_severity.description: Severity classification for violations under different evaluation modes.

full_mode.description: Violation severity in Full mode (N=30) when effect_size >= effect_size_threshold.

full_mode_below_effect_size_threshold.description: Violation severity in Full mode when p < p_value_threshold but effect_size < effect_size_threshold (statistically significant but practically negligible).

evaluation_mode_applicability.description: Which evaluation modes this MR is checked in.

calibration_status.description: Whether this MR tolerance has been empirically calibrated against real output pairs or is analytically derived. Analytically derived tolerances should be updated after collecting 100+ real output pairs per FM-009 mitigation.

calibration_notes.description: Notes on calibration history, including date of last calibration and number of pairs evaluated.

source.description: Reference to the behavioral-contracts.md section that defines this MR tolerance.

related_failure_modes.description: ADR-001 failure mode IDs that this MR tolerance addresses.

examples.name: Paraphrase Consistency
examples.definition: Paraphrasing the user-facing portion of a system prompt (not structural constraints or tools list) should not change output quality by more than 0.05. A well-functioning agent produces equivalent-quality output regardless of surface-level wording variation in the task description.

transformation.description: Replace the task description portion of the user message with a semantically equivalent paraphrase generated by a secondary LLM call with explicit instruction to preserve meaning and intent.
transformation.preservation_requirement: Semantic intent and factual content are preserved; only surface wording varies

examples.max_delta_rationale: LLM non-determinism baseline is 0.02-0.04 standard deviation at temperature=0. Allowing 0.05 gives approximately one standard deviation of buffer above the non-determinism floor. Derived from LLMORPH's 8.6% false positive rate at similar tolerances across 560K tests (ASE 2025). Paraphrase transformations that preserve intent should not change quality beyond measurement noise.

conditions.description: Wilcoxon signed-rank test is statistically significant
Mean absolute delta exceeds practical significance threshold

examples.calibration_notes: Initial tolerance analytically derived from LLMORPH baseline. Requires empirical calibration against 100+ real Jerry agent output pairs per FM-009 mitigation plan.
